'''Kyriacos Costa Nicolaou''' ({{langx|el|Κυριάκος Κ. Νικολάου}}; born 5 July 1946)<ref>{{cite web | title=Rice University | website=The People of Rice | date=1946-07-05 | url=https://profiles.rice.edu/faculty/kc-nicolaou | access-date=2025-04-25}}</ref> is a Greek Cypriot-American chemist known for his research in the area of [[natural product]]s [[total synthesis]]. He is currently Harry C. and Olga K. Wiess Professor of Chemistry at [[Rice University]], having previously held academic positions at [[The Scripps Research Institute]]/[[UC San Diego]] and the [[University of Pennsylvania]].<ref>{{cite web | title= Full CV of Dr. K.C. Nicolaou| url=https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Nicolaou_Kyriacos_Costa_EN.pdf | access-date=2025-04-25}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/new-fellows-2013/|title=New Fellows 2013|publisher=Royal Society|accessdate = 30 July 2013}}</ref>

==Biography==
K. C. Nicolaou was born on July 5, 1946, in [[Karavas]], Cyprus where he grew up and went to school until the age of 18.  In 1964, he went to England where he spent two years learning English and preparing to enter University. He studied chemistry at the [[University of London]] (B.Sc., 1969, [[Bedford College (London)|Bedford College]]; [[Ph.D.]] 1972, [[University College London]], with Professors F. Sondheimer and P. J. Garratt).  In 1972, he moved to the United States and, after postdoctoral appointments at [[Columbia University]] (1972–1973, Professor T. J. Katz) and [[Harvard University]] (1973–1976, Professor [[E. J. Corey]]), he joined the faculty at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] where he became the Rhodes-Thompson Professor of Chemistry. While at Penn, he won the [[Sloan Fellowship]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://chemistry.rice.edu/people/kc-nicolaou|title=K.C. Nicolaou|access-date=May 27, 2020|archive-date=August 13, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200813022617/https://chemistry.rice.edu/people/kc-nicolaou|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 1989, he relocated to San Diego, where he took up a joint appointment at the [[University of California]], [[San Diego]], where he served as Professor of Chemistry, and [[The Scripps Research Institute]], where he was Darlene Shiley Professor of Chemistry and Chairman of the Department of Chemistry. In 1996, he was appointed Aline W. and L.S. Skaggs Professor of Chemical Biology in The Skaggs Institute for Chemical Biology, The Scripps Research Institute. From 2005 to 2011, he directed Chemical Synthesis Laboratory @ ICES-A*STAR, Singapore. In 2013, Nicolaou moved to [[Rice University]].

The Nicolaou group is active in the field of [[organic chemistry]] with research interests in methodology development and [[total synthesis]].
<ref>{{cite news|last=Borman|first=Stu|title=Total Synthesis of Anticancer Agent Taxol Achieved by Two Different Routes|url=http://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/cen-v072n008.p032|accessdate=22 August 2013|newspaper=Chemical & Engineering News|date=21 February 1994}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Blakeslee|first=Sandra|title=Race to Synthesize Cancer Drug Molecule Has Photo Finish|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1994/02/15/science/race-to-synthesize-cancer-drug-molecule-has-photo-finish.html|accessdate=22 August 2013|newspaper=The New York Times|date=15 February 1994}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/arthur-c-cope-award.html| title= Arthur C. Cope Award|publisher= ACS|accessdate = 19 January 2015}} </ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/new-fellows-2013/|title=New Fellows 2013|publisher=Royal Society|accessdate = 30 July 2013}}</ref> He is responsible for the synthesis of many complex molecules found in nature, such as [[Taxol]] and [[vancomycin]]. His group's route to [[Taxol]], completed in 1994 at roughly the same time as a [[Holton Taxol total synthesis|synthesis]] by the group of [[Robert A. Holton]], attracted national [[news media]] attention due to [[Taxol]]'s structural complexity and its potent anti-cancer activity.<ref>{{cite news|last=Borman|first=Stu|title=Total Synthesis of Anticancer Agent Taxol Achieved by Two Different Routes|newspaper=Chemical & Engineering News|date=February 21, 1994|volume=72 |issue=8 |pages=32–34 |doi=10.1021/cen-v072n008.p032}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Blakeslee|first=Sandra|title=Race to Synthesize Cancer Drug Molecule Has Photo Finish|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1994/02/15/science/race-to-synthesize-cancer-drug-molecule-has-photo-finish.html|access-date=August 22, 2013|newspaper=The New York Times|date=February 15, 1994}}</ref>

==Total syntheses accomplished==
{{div col}}
*[[Endiandric acid c|Endiandric acids A]]–[[Endiandric acid c|D]] (1982)
*[[Amphoteronolide B]] and [[Amphotericin B]] (1987)
*[[Calicheamicin|Calicheamicin γ<sub>1</sub>]] (1992)
*[[Sirolimus]] (1993)
*[[Nicolaou Taxol total synthesis|Taxol]] (1994)
*[[Zaragozic acid|Zaragozic acid A]] (1994)
*[[Brevetoxin|Brevetoxin B]] (1995)
*[[Vancomycin]] (1998)
*[[Uncialamycin]] (2008)
*[[Sporolides|Sporolide B]] (2009)
*[[Viridicatumtoxin B]] (2013)
*[[Shishijimicin A]] (2015)
*[[Thailanstatin A]] (2016)
*[[Gukulenin B]] (2022)
{{div col end}}

==Books==
He is also the co-author of four popular books on [[total synthesis]]: 
#Classics in Total Synthesis I, 1996{{Ref|Classics1}}
#Classics in Total Synthesis II, 2003{{Ref|Classics2}}
#Classics in Total Synthesis III, 2011{{Ref|Classics3}}
#Classics in Total Synthesis IV, 2025{{Ref|Classics4}}

Additionally, he authored or co-authored several other books:
#Molecules That Changed the World, 2008
#Handbook of Combinatorial Chemistry: Drugs, Catalysts, Materials, 2002
#Selenium in Natural Products Synthesis, 1984

== Awards ==
K. C. Nicolaou has received numerous awards and honors including:

{{div col}}
* 2021 [[Robert Koch Gold Medal]] (Germany)
* 2016 [[Wolf Prize in Chemistry]] (Israel)
* 2011 [[Benjamin Franklin Medal (Franklin Institute)|Benjamin Franklin Medal]] in Chemistry ([[Franklin Institute]] USA){{Ref|FranklinMedal}}
* 2005 [[Arthur C. Cope Award]] (USA)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/arthur-c-cope-award.html| title= Arthur C. Cope Award|publisher= ACS|access-date = January 19, 2015}}</ref>
* 2003 Nobel Laureate Signature Award in Graduate Education (with [[Phil S. Baran]])
* 2002 [[Tetrahedron Prize]]
* 2001 [[Ernst Schering Prize]] (Germany)
* 2000 [[Paul Karrer Gold Medal]] (Switzerland)
* 1998 [[Gustavus Esselen#Esselen Award|Esselen Award]] (USA)
* 1996 [[Linus Pauling Award]] (USA)
* 1996 [[William H. Nichols Medal]] (USA)
* Aspirin Prize (Spain)
* Max Tishler Prize Lecture (Harvard)
* Yamada Prize (Japan)
* Janssen Prize (Belgium)
* Nagoya Medal (Japan)
* Centenary Medal ([[Royal Society]] UK)
* Inhoffen Medal (Germany)
* ACS Award for Creative Work in Synthetic Organic Chemistry (USA)
* ACS Guenther Award in Natural Products Chemistry (USA)
* Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]
* Member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]]
*Member of the [[American Philosophical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Member History|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Kyriacos+C.+Nicolaou&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|access-date=April 2, 2021|website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref>
* [[Foreign Member of the Royal Society]] (2013)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/new-fellows-2013/|title=New Fellows 2013|publisher=Royal Society|access-date = July 30, 2013}}</ref>
* Several honorary degrees
{{div col end}}
